source_text: Sed hactenus de materia praesenti. Satis iam enim arbitror instructam esse carnis in Christo et ex virgine natae et humanae probationem. Quod et solum discussum sufficere potuisset, citra singularunm ex diverse opinionum congressionem quam et argumentationibus earum et scripturis, quibus utuntur, provocavimus ex abundanti, uti eo quod probavimus quid et unde fuerit Christi caro quid non fuerit adversus omnes praeiudicaverimus. Ut autem clausulam de praefatione communi faciat resurrectio nostrae carnis alio libello defendenda, hic habebit praestructionem, manifesto iam quale fuerit quod in Christo resurrexit.
thought_title: Closing summary of the proof of Christ's flesh
orientation: Tertullian is concluding his argument that Christ's flesh was truly born of the Virgin and truly human, and he is preparing to hand over the topic of the resurrection of our flesh to another treatise.
pass_a_gloss: But thus far about the present matter. For I think that the proof of the flesh in Christ, both born of the virgin and human, has now been sufficiently established. Which even if it alone had been discussed, it could have sufficed, apart from the encounter with the individual diverse opinions, which we have also challenged from abundance both by their arguments and by the scriptures which they use, so that by that which we have proved, what the flesh of Christ was and whence it was, we have already decided in advance against all what it was not. But so that the resurrection of our flesh, to be defended in another little book, may make a closing of the common preface, it will have here a preliminary construction, since it is now manifest what sort of thing that was which rose again in Christ.

choices.term: carnis in Christo et ex virgine natae et humanae
choices.english: of the flesh in Christ, both born of the virgin and human
choices.why: Keeps the two coordinated adjectives 'born of the virgin' and 'human' modifying 'flesh' in the same order as the Latin, preserving the double proof Tertullian claims to have established.
rejected: of the human flesh in Christ born of the virgin
of Christ's flesh as born of the virgin and as human

choices.term: citra singularum ex diversis opinionum congressionem
choices.english: apart from the encounter with the individual diverse opinions
choices.why: Renders 'citra' as 'apart from' to show that the single discussion would have sufficed even without engaging each opinion, and keeps 'congressionem' as 'encounter' to preserve the combative tone.
rejected: without the conflict of the various individual opinions
short of the engagement with each of the diverse opinions

choices.english: we have also challenged from abundance
choices.why: Keeps the legal-rhetorical force of 'provocare' as 'challenge' and renders 'ex abundanti' literally as 'from abundance' to preserve the sense of doing more than was necessary.
rejected: we have called out as an extra

choices.term: quid et unde fuerit Christi caro quid non fuerit
choices.english: what the flesh of Christ was and whence it was, what it was not
choices.why: Preserves the exact threefold question pattern (what, whence, what not) in the same order as the Latin, which is the logical structure of Tertullian's proof.
rejected: what Christ's flesh was, where it came from, and what it was not
the nature and origin of Christ's flesh and what it was not

choices.why: Renders the rare noun 'praestructio' literally as 'preliminary construction' to preserve the architectural metaphor of laying a foundation for the next treatise.

choices.term: manifesto iam quale fuerit quod in Christo resurrexit
choices.english: since it is now manifest what sort of thing that was which rose again in Christ
choices.why: Keeps 'manifesto' as an ablative absolute 'since it is now manifest' and preserves the indirect question 'quale fuerit' as 'what sort of thing that was' to maintain the precise logical connection to the resurrection.
rejected: it being now evident what kind of thing rose in Christ
now that it is clear what it was that rose in Christ

pass_b_english: But enough has been said on the present subject. I think the proof has now been sufficiently established that the flesh in Christ was both born of the virgin and human. This proof alone, once discussed, could have sufficed, apart from the clash with each of the diverse opinions, which we have provoked over and above what was needed with their arguments and the Scriptures they use, so that by what we have proved—what the flesh of Christ was and whence it was, what it was not—we have decided in advance against all of them. But so that the resurrection of our flesh, which must be defended in another little book, may form the conclusion of this common preface, it will have here its preliminary construction, since it is now manifest what sort of thing that was which rose again in Christ.

problems.quote: This single discussion could have sufficed on its own, apart from the encounter with the individual diverse opinions, whose arguments and the Scriptures they use we have also challenged from abundance
problems.source_quote: Quod et solum discussum sufficere potuisset, citra singularunm ex diverse opinionum congressionem quam et argumentationibus earum et scripturis, quibus utuntur, provocavimus ex abundanti
problems.why: Sense muddled: the proof alone would have sufficed even without the extra engagement with each opinion, which we undertook over and above what was needed. 'Encounter' and the relative clause are unclear.
problems.fix: This proof alone, once examined, could have sufficed, even without the clash with each separate opinion, which we have also provoked, over and above need, by their arguments and by the Scriptures they use.

edits.old: This single discussion could have sufficed on its own, apart from the encounter with the individual diverse opinions, whose arguments and the Scriptures they use we have also challenged from abundance
edits.new: This proof alone, once discussed, could have sufficed, apart from the clash with each of the diverse opinions, which we have provoked over and above what was needed with their arguments and the Scriptures they use

fixed: Fixed mistranslation of 'Quod et solum discussum...provocavimus ex abundanti': subject is the proof alone discussed, 'quam...provocavimus' is the clash provoked by means of their arguments/Scriptures, 'ex abundanti' is supererogatory, not challenged from abundance.

last_rejected.quote: the clash with each of the diverse opinions
last_rejected.source_quote: citra singularunm ex diverse opinionum congressionem
last_rejected.why: ex diverso means from the opposite side, not that the opinions are diverse. The preposition is dropped.
last_rejected.fix: apart from engaging each of the opinions from the other side
last_rejected.ruling: "ex diverso opinionum" rendered "diverse opinions" loses the 'opposing' nuance. But "each of the diverse opinions" still conveys the sense (the various rival views), so the meaning is not materially changed.
